short: Unitary synthesis from a Boolean oracle

title.title: Polynomial-time unitary synthesis from a Boolean oracle
title.subtitle: Claim: one uniform polynomial oracle circuit reaches every $n$-qubit unitary within diamond distance $1/2$

object.caption: gates from $\{H, T, T^\dagger, \mathrm{CNOT}\}$ and calls to a Boolean oracle $\mathcal O$

beats.text: A circuit generated in polynomial time from $n$ alone, with Boolean oracle calls
The oracle is chosen for the target unitary $U$; the circuit is not
Claim: it reaches every $n$-qubit $U$ within diamond distance $1/2$

achievement.label: Unitary synthesis problem (Aaronson–Kuperberg 2007)
statement: \exists f:\ \lVert C^{f}_n - U \rVert_\diamond \le \tfrac{1}{2} \text{ for every } n\text{-qubit } U
achievement.context: Before: a one-query lower bound (Lombardi–Ma–Wright, STOC 2024)
achievement.note: Constant error only; building the oracle efficiently is not claimed

verify.ourCheck: We read the papers' claims and caveats; we did not referee them

plain: Give a quantum computer a cleverly chosen classical lookup table, and a short circuit can mimic any operation

voice.text: A circuit built in polynomial time from the input size alone, calling a Boolean oracle;
only the oracle depends on the target.
Claimed: within diamond distance one half of every unitary.
